summary: This CSS file styles two notice components—one for old posts and one for reviewed posts—by composing them from a global design system's callout styles. Each notice gets its own color variant (warning or tip) and standard spacing, while the body text inside has specific sizing and line-height to keep things readable.

explanations.13: The 'composes' keyword brings in styles from another CSS module or global styles—it's like inheriting base callout styling that's defined elsewhere.
explanations.14: This composes another set of styles specifically for the warning variant of callouts, giving this notice its distinctive warning appearance.
explanations.19: Similar to line 13, but this time for the 'reviewedPostNotice', pulling in the base callout styles.
explanations.20: This adds the 'tip' variant styles instead of warning, so reviewed notices look different visually.
explanations.29: min-width: 0 is a trick that forces the element to respect its content's actual width instead of stretching to fill available space—useful when text needs to wrap or truncate.
explanations.31: Setting font-size to 0.95rem makes the notice text slightly smaller than the default, creating visual hierarchy.
